subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept arbitrary bootstrap context files, and if so should the supported shape be exact session-scoped entries rather than global arbitrary `paths`?
rationale: This changes prompt/session context behavior and operator config semantics, so the safe default and supported contract need maintainer intent before a fix lands.

options.title: Sponsor session-scoped guarded config
options.body: Rebase and review the linked PR or an equivalent patch that keeps global paths allowlisted and permits custom basenames only through explicit exact-session entries.

options.title: Allow global arbitrary paths
options.body: Accept the broader original request by making existing `paths` able to load any workspace-contained file, trading simplicity for higher accidental injection risk.

options.title: Reject core expansion
options.body: Keep core bootstrap filenames fixed and direct custom context needs to workspace hooks, plugin hooks, or context-engine plugins instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor session-scoped guarded config
recommendation.body: Rebase and review the linked PR or an equivalent patch that keeps global paths allowlisted and permits custom basenames only through explicit exact-session entries.

likelyOwner.reason: He moved this behavior into the bundled hook and worked on boundary-safe bootstrap reads, making him the best history-backed owner for the product-shape call.
